Actuation B (OUT=B): Main spool shifts to connect P to B and A to T; flow goes out port B and returns from port A; pressure on port B is limited by its relief valve to 100.

flow_scenarios: Neutral: Solenoids de-energized, spool spring-centered. Supply P is blocked at the spool. Work ports A and B are open to tank T.

Energized for Port A: Spool shifts to direct flow from P through the compensator to port A. Return flow from port B is directed to tank T. Maximum pressure on port A is limited by the shock valve to 250.

Energized for Port B: Spool shifts to direct flow from P through the compensator to port B. Return flow from port A is directed to tank T. Maximum pressure on port B is limited by the shock valve to 225.
Cavitation prevention: If pressure at port A or B drops below tank pressure, the anti-cavitation check valves allow makeup fluid to flow from T into the respective work port.

flow_scenarios: Neutral: Spool in spring-centered position, P is blocked, work ports A and B are open to the T return rail (open neutral).
Actuated Envelope 2: P connects to A, B connects to T. Flow is regulated by the upstream pressure compensator.
Actuated Envelope 4 (Bottom): P connects to B, A connects to T.
Actuated Envelope 1 (Top): Float position; connects work ports A and B together and to tank.
Overpressure Port A: If pressure on A exceeds 250, the shock relief valve opens to vent fluid to the T rail.
Overpressure Port B: If pressure on B exceeds 225, the shock relief valve opens to vent fluid to the T rail.
Cavitation: If pressure at port A or B drops below tank pressure, the corresponding anti-cavitation check valve opens to draw fluid from the T rail.
